column2: “勿以太平而忘武备”。清顺治时一座射殿出现在奉先殿前，弓马骑射成为清代武备的核心。康熙帝曾亲率诸皇子和善射侍卫于此射箭，雍正时改为箭亭，乾隆帝在此召见殿试弓马成绩最优秀的武进士，嘉庆时箭亭亦被开辟为弓刀石的考试场地。

column4: "Do not forget military readiness in time of peace." Under the Shunzhi Emperor an archery hall stood before the Hall of Ancestral Worship, and mounted archery became the core of Qing military training. The Kangxi Emperor personally led the princes and skilled guards in archery here; under Yongzheng it was renamed the Arrow Pavilion; the Qianlong Emperor received here the military graduates who had excelled in the palace examination in riding and archery; and by the Jiaqing reign the pavilion also served as the examination ground for bow, sabre and stone-lifting.

column2: 故宫博物院收藏的清代宫廷珍宝，大部分出自紫禁城内掌管营造的造办处奉旨制作，还有一些是逢年节庆典时地方官吏的朝贡品。这些珍宝大都选用金、银、玉、翠、珍珠及各种宝石等名贵材质，征调各地著名匠师设计制造，竭尽巧思、不惜工本，一器之成往往经年累月，其工艺代表了当时的最高水平。

column4: Qing court treasures in the Palace Museum, most made to imperial order by the Imperial Household Workshops within the Forbidden City, with some presented as tribute by provincial officials at festivals and celebrations. Almost all use precious materials — gold, silver, jade, jadeite, pearls and assorted gemstones — and were designed and made by leading craftsmen summoned from across the empire, sparing neither ingenuity nor expense; a single object could take years to complete, and the workmanship represents the highest standard of its day.

column2: 故宫博物院收藏陶瓷类文物约 35 万件，绝大部分属原清宫旧藏，自成体系、流传有绪。本馆从中遴选 400 多件精品，按时代发展顺序展示，涵盖从红陶、灰陶、彩陶、黑陶、白陶到原始瓷、青瓷、黑瓷、白瓷以及颜色釉瓷和釉下彩、釉上彩瓷器，呈现中国陶瓷一万多年绵延不断的发展历程。陈列于武英殿正殿、工字廊与后殿敬思殿。

column4: The Palace Museum holds some 350,000 ceramic objects, the great majority from the former Qing court collection, forming a coherent body with a documented line of transmission. More than 400 of the finest are shown here in chronological order, covering red, grey, painted, black and white earthenware, proto-porcelain, celadon, black ware, white ware, monochrome glazes and underglaze- and overglaze-painted porcelain, presenting more than ten thousand years of continuous Chinese ceramic development. Displayed in the main hall of the Hall of Martial Valour, the I-shaped corridor and the rear Jingsi Hall.

column2: 故宫雕塑馆陈列在慈宁宫内，分雕塑荟萃馆、汉唐陶俑馆、砖石画像馆、修德白石馆、佛教造像馆五部分，陈列面积约 1375 平方米，展品总数 425 件。涵盖陶俑、画像砖石、佛像三大类：陶俑自战国至明代前后相续；陕北与晋西南画像石造型独特；河北曲阳白石佛像自北魏至隋唐纪年有序；宫廷旧藏中的永乐、宣德款藏传佛教铜造像体现明初宫廷风格，清代六世班禅像为清宫藏传佛教造像代表作。

column4: The Palace Museum's Sculpture Gallery, housed in the Palace of Compassion and Tranquillity, comprises five sections — sculpture highlights, Han and Tang pottery figures, pictorial bricks and stones, Quyang white marble, and Buddhist images — with about 1,375 square metres of display space and 425 objects. It covers three main categories: pottery figures running continuously from the Warring States to the Ming; the distinctive pictorial stones of northern Shaanxi and south-western Shanxi; the white marble Buddhas of Quyang, Hebei, securely dated from the Northern Wei through the Sui and Tang; and, from the former palace collection, Yongle- and Xuande-marked Tibetan Buddhist bronzes exemplifying early Ming court style, with the Qing image of the Sixth Panchen Lama representing Qing court Tibetan Buddhist sculpture.

Most are British, with others from France and Switzerland, and some made in Guangzhou, Suzhou and the palace clock workshop. Besides striking the hours and quarters, they use linked mechanisms to set figures, birds, beasts and flowers in continuous motion. The finest are selected for display here.

column3: 该展厅的核心展品，超真人尺度的彩绘木雕观音，以“自在坐”（royal ease）姿态呈现：一腿垂下、一手松搭膝上，神情从容含笑，是同期造像中极罕见的松弛姿态。1920 年起在 MFA 展出，1999 年入库，经一年半修复后于 2016 年重新亮相。修复中动用了紫外成像、X 光与碳十四测年。Hervey Edward Wetzel 基金购藏，编号 20.590。
column4: The core object in this gallery, a larger-than-life painted wood sculpture of Guanyin, presented in the “royal ease” posture: one leg lowered and one hand resting loosely on the knee, with a composed, smiling expression. This exceptionally relaxed posture is extremely rare among sculptures of the same period. Exhibited at the MFA from 1920, it entered the collection in 1999 and reappeared in 2016 after a year and a half of conservation. Ultraviolet imaging, X-rays, and radiocarbon dating were used during the conservation. Purchased with funds from the Hervey Edward Wetzel Fund, accession number 20.590.

column2: 北宋宫廷御用的汝窑瓷，淡天青釉。汝窑存世量极少，全世界不足一百件，此盘是 MFA 中国陶瓷收藏的顶级重器。
column3: 北宋宫廷御用的汝窑瓷，淡天青釉。汝窑存世量极少，全世界不足一百件，此盘是 MFA 中国陶瓷收藏的顶级重器。
column4: A Ru ware vessel made for the imperial court of the Northern Song dynasty, with a pale sky-blue glaze. Very few Ru ware objects survive; fewer than one hundred are known worldwide. This dish is a masterpiece of the MFA’s Chinese ceramics collection.

column2: 元末画家周砥的水墨山水手卷，其克制的笔法影响了后世数代文人画家。同一手卷中还有明代沈周观此画后所作的另一段山水回应，展厅配有互动屏可展开全卷比对。
column3: 元末画家周砥的水墨山水手卷，其克制的笔法影响了后世数代文人画家。同一手卷中还有明代沈周观此画后所作的另一段山水回应，展厅配有互动屏可展开全卷比对。
column4: An ink landscape handscroll by the late Yuan painter Zhou Di, whose restrained brushwork influenced generations of literati painters. The same handscroll also contains another landscape response made by the Ming painter Shen Zhou after viewing this painting. An interactive screen in the gallery allows visitors to open and compare the entire scroll.

column2: 罗汉是证得觉悟的佛陀弟子。此件与展厅内两幅寺庙绘画一同展出，用以说明佛教如何渗入中国日常生活。
column3: 罗汉是证得觉悟的佛陀弟子。此件与展厅内两幅寺庙绘画一同展出，用以说明佛教如何渗入中国日常生活。
column4: An arhat is a disciple of the Buddha who has attained enlightenment. This object is displayed together with two temple paintings in the gallery to illustrate how Buddhism became integrated into daily life in China.

column2: 寺庙厅的视觉焦点，密教万神殿的至高神，双手结“智拳印”象征神圣智慧。寺庙厅设计于 1909 年，日美工匠参照奈良法隆寺八世纪伽蓝的图纸，用巨大木柱与日式斗栱营造出置身古寺的氛围，配以幽暗照明供人静观。
column3: 寺庙厅的视觉焦点，密教万神殿的至高神，双手结“智拳印”象征神圣智慧。寺庙厅设计于 1909 年，日美工匠参照奈良法隆寺八世纪伽蓝的图纸，用巨大木柱与日式斗栱营造出置身古寺的氛围，配以幽暗照明供人静观。
column4: The visual focus of the Temple Hall, the supreme deity of the Esoteric Buddhist pantheon, with both hands forming the “wisdom fist” mudra, symbolizing sacred wisdom. Designed in 1909, the Temple Hall was constructed by Japanese and American artisans according to plans of the eighth-century temple complex at Hōryūji in Nara. Its massive wooden columns and Japanese-style bracket sets create the atmosphere of being inside an ancient temple, with subdued lighting for quiet contemplation.

column2: 位于主尊大日如来右侧。寺庙厅内共供奉七尊日本佛像，材质为桧木或樟木，部分施彩或贴金。
column3: 位于主尊大日如来右侧。寺庙厅内共供奉七尊日本佛像，材质为桧木或樟木，部分施彩或贴金。
column4: Located to the right of the principal image, Dainichi Nyorai. Seven Japanese Buddhist sculptures are enshrined in the Temple Hall; they are made of hinoki or camphor wood, and some are painted or gilded.

column4: The earliest group of sculptures in the Temple Hall, dating to the early Heian period of the ninth century. The Four Heavenly Kings are guardians of the Buddhist law; two of them are displayed here.

column2: 密教五大明王之首，忿怒相，持剑与羂索。与毗沙门天同为寺庙厅的重要造像。
column3: 密教五大明王之首，忿怒相，持剑与羂索。与毗沙门天同为寺庙厅的重要造像。
column4: The foremost of the Five Wisdom Kings of Esoteric Buddhism, shown in wrathful form and holding a sword and a noose. Together with Bishamonten, it is one of the important sculptures in the Temple Hall.

column2: 四天王中的北方守护神，亦为日本七福神之一。2022 年前后七尊佛像曾移至公开修复工作室做“Conservation in Action”项目，修复后归位寺庙厅。
column3: 四天王中的北方守护神，亦为日本七福神之一。2022 年前后七尊佛像曾移至公开修复工作室做“Conservation in Action”项目，修复后归位寺庙厅。
column4: The northern guardian among the Four Heavenly Kings, and also one of the Seven Lucky Gods of Japan. Around 2022, the seven Buddhist sculptures were moved to a public conservation studio for the “Conservation in Action” project and returned to the Temple Hall after conservation.

column2: 镰仓时代大佛师快庆 1189 年所作的弥勒（未来佛）像，原供奉于奈良兴福寺，1906 年由该寺售出，1920 年入藏 MFA。像高约 142 厘米，是快庆有明确纪年的早期代表作。编号 20.723.1。
column3: 镰仓时代大佛师快庆 1189 年所作的弥勒（未来佛）像，原供奉于奈良兴福寺，1906 年由该寺售出，1920 年入藏 MFA。像高约 142 厘米，是快庆有明确纪年的早期代表作。编号 20.723.1。
column4: A sculpture of Maitreya, the Future Buddha, made in 1189 by Kaikei, the great sculptor of the Kamakura period. Originally enshrined at Kōfukuji in Nara, it was sold by the temple in 1906 and entered the MFA collection in 1920. Approximately 142 centimeters high, it is an early representative work by Kaikei with a definite date. Accession number 20.723.1.

column2: 江户奇想派画家曾我蕭白的巨作，1911 年入藏 MFA。修复后恢复为原本的八面隔扇（襖絵）形制，是入馆以来首次以原貌呈现。
column3: 江户奇想派画家曾我蕭白的巨作，1911 年入藏 MFA。修复后恢复为原本的八面隔扇（襖絵）形制，是入馆以来首次以原貌呈现。
column4: A monumental work by Soga Shōhaku, a painter of the Edo-period eccentric school, acquired by the MFA in 1911. After conservation, it was restored to its original form as an eight-panel set of sliding-door paintings (fusuma-e), and is being presented in its original appearance for the first time since entering the museum.

column2: 改造后的日本艺术展厅内复原了传统茶室，配榻榻米与壁龛。MFA 的日本收藏 1890 年设立，是全美首个此类部门，现藏约 10 万件；浮世绘版画逾 5 万张，为日本境外最大，因避光需要每半年轮换一次主题展。
column3: 改造后的日本艺术展厅内复原了传统茶室，配榻榻米与壁龛。MFA 的日本收藏 1890 年设立，是全美首个此类部门，现藏约 10 万件；浮世绘版画逾 5 万张，为日本境外最大，因避光需要每半年轮换一次主题展。
column4: The renovated Japanese art galleries recreate a traditional tea room with tatami mats and a tokonoma alcove. The MFA’s Japanese collection was established in 1890 as the first department of its kind in the United States and now comprises approximately 100,000 objects. With more than 50,000 ukiyo-e prints, it is the largest collection outside Japan; because of light sensitivity, thematic exhibitions are rotated every six months.
